newsitem.title: USA: Nasdaq slips, follows decline in bond market.
newsitem.headline: Nasdaq slips, follows decline in bond market.

text.p: Weakness in the bond market and tepid interest in technology stocks pressured Nasdaq shares Thursday, traders said.

The Nasdaq composite index lost 18.17 points or 1.33 percent to 1347.41. The Dow industrials shed 93 points or 1.32 percent to 6927. The benchmark long-bond slipped almost a point to yield 6.65 percent.
"When stocks failed to rally in the morning, investors needed direction. They looked to the bond market, which weakened, and that pull stocks down further," one trader said.
Other traders said profit taking in semiconductor stocks pushed the Nasdaq index lower.

Cyrix Corp gained 3-7/8 to 29-3/8 after it said it will supply Compaq Computer Corp with a new low-cost microprocessor for personal computers. Intel Corp, the dominate PC microprocessor maker, dropped 4 to 149-7/8.

AMERCO Inc dropped 6-7/8 to 28-1/8 after its disappointing third quarter report. Vivus Inc also dropped 3-3/8 to 74-3/4 after CS First Boston cut the stock to a hold from a buy. Overall, losers beat gained 2725 to 1715 on total volume of 624 million shares.
